Man dragged by vehicle, robbed in Waterloo: police

By Christine Clark

Posted Oct 20, 2026 07:08:40 AM.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:21
Instaread

The Waterloo Regional Police Service (WRPS) is looking into an incident in Waterloo that saw a man dragged by a vehicle and reportedly robbed of some his clothing and belongings.

Saturday, Oct. 17 police were called to the Meaford Drive and Chelford Crescent of the city, not too far from University Avenue and Hwy. 85.

Police said a witness, who was hiding in the trees at the time, reported a man was crawling shirtless across a front lawn. That man had told the witness he was just robbed and was searching for his belongings.

He left before police arrived shortly after 7 p.m.

Related:

  • Arrest made following restaurant robbery near Fairview Park Mall
  • Person hit in face with piece of wood in downtown robbery: police
  • CCTV cameras used in 19 cases, more to be switched on in K-W, Cambridge

After looking into the incident further, police believed the man had been dragged by a vehicle before he was reportedly robbed.

“Through the investigation, officers determined that the victim had been dragged by a white four-door hatchback on Meaford Drive,” said police.

“During the incident, an unknown suspect exited the vehicle and stole the victim’s backpack and sweater while an altercation was taking place.”

The victim in question was described as a white man in his late 30s. He had not been found by police as of Tuesday morning.

There were no suspect descriptions released by WRPS.

Anyone with information is asked to contact police.
